Lab pathway

Safety boundaryThis practice lab teaches communication and workflow recognition. It never asks a service representative to diagnose or give clinical advice.
01 · Signal brief

Patient Communication and Workflow Recognition

Practice identifying the request, emotional cues, process triggers, and required next action across communication channels.

Start with the communication channel

Communication Evidence by Channel

Select a channel and review the communication evidence available in that setting.

Core conversation model

HEAR Communication Framework

The first response should lower friction and produce the information needed for the next safe action.

H
Hear

Let the caller finish. Listen for the stated request and the unstated concern.

E
Empathize

Name the concern without making promises you cannot keep.

A
Act

Use the approved workflow, verification steps, and escalation trigger.

R
Recap

Confirm the next step, check understanding, and document the disposition.

Trigger studio

Trigger Categories and Signal Classification

A trigger is information that changes the ordinary workflow. Explore each category, then practice recognizing it inside natural language.

Signal sort

What changes the workflow?

Choose the trigger category, or choose “routine” when no override is present.
Language lab

Therapeutic Language Evaluation

Choose a phrase, decide whether it is effective, risky, or needs revision, then compare your reasoning with the coaching.

Phrase 1 of 6
Context practice

Therapeutic Response Selection

Choose the response that acknowledges emotion, stays within role, and moves toward an approved next step. All options are intentionally similar in length.

Practice 1 of 5

Which response is most therapeutic?

Compare acknowledgment, role boundaries, and the next action.

04 · QA audit

Quality Review and Coaching Analysis

05 · Final assessment

Integrated Communication Decision Assessment

Apply communication, trigger recognition, routing, role boundaries, and quality standards without coaching until each answer is submitted.

Assessment standard

Evidence Before Action

Questions appear in a new order for each attempt. Answer choices are also randomized and written at comparable lengths.

Question 1 of 8

One best answer is supported by the communication evidence and approved process.
